name: Kinder Morgan
description: Kinder Morgan is a toll-road business for energy: it owns or operates about 78,000 miles of pipelines, 136 terminals and more than 700 Bcf of gas storage (Dec 2025). About two thirds of its segment earnings come from natural gas pipelines that move gas from shale fields to power plants, utilities, factories and LNG export plants under long-term fixed-fee contracts, so profit depends far more on volumes shipped and contract rates than on the gas price. The rest comes from refined-product and crude pipelines, storage terminals (liquids and bulk, including ships and rail) and a CO2 business that sells carbon dioxide and some oil. Growth now comes from new pipelines to feed LNG exports and power demand (Trident, Mississippi Crossing, SSE4). It paid dividends of 1.17 dollars per share in 2025 and plans 1.19 dollars for 2026.

businessLines.name: Natural Gas Pipelines
businessLines.shareBasis: 11,009 of 16,937 million consolidated revenues (segments sum to 16,969 before eliminations)
businessLines.how: Long-term fixed reservation fees from customers who reserve pipeline or storage space, plus smaller volume-based fees and some gas sales; commodity price is a minor driver, revenue mostly moves with contracted capacity and new expansions.
businessLines.description: About 42,000 miles of wholly owned gas pipelines plus equity interests in about 25,000 more (Tennessee Gas, El Paso Natural Gas, Southern Natural Gas, NGPL, Florida Gas and Texas intrastate systems), gas storage, gathering and processing, and LNG services.

businessLines.name: Products Pipelines
businessLines.how: Pipeline tariffs per barrel moved plus terminal fees; revenue follows fuel volumes and regulated rate increases.
businessLines.description: Refined-product pipelines (gasoline, diesel, jet), NGL and crude pipelines, and their terminals, including Bakken crude assets and West Coast systems.

businessLines.name: Terminals
businessLines.how: Storage and handling fees under multi-year contracts, plus throughput and ship charters.
businessLines.description: Liquids terminals (storage tanks for oil products and chemicals) and bulk terminals (coal, petcoke, steel, aggregates), including Jones Act tankers.

businessLines.name: CO2
businessLines.how: CO2 sales under contract and oil sales from its own fields, the only line of KMI with direct oil price exposure.
businessLines.description: Sells carbon dioxide used to push oil out of aging fields and owns interests in Permian oil fields and CO2 and crude pipelines.
